title: US-short §13 lifecycle threshold authority — the machine-readable §13.2 thresholds + §13.1 item→category map the lifecycle eval DERIVES each item's review threshold from (so the mutable register can't self-author it)
description: Batch-3 R2 governance contract (design §13.2 / §13.1). The §13.2 reminder thresholds are prose; this authority pins them machine-readably PER CATEGORY (count_type / min_count / secondary_required) and governs each §13.1 calibration item's category. engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval.py reads it as the threshold AUTHORITY: the lifecycle_register no longer carries threshold metadata, so it cannot lower its own bar (R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-THRESHOLD-SELF-AUTHORING-BYPASS). BOTH the 7 category thresholds AND the full 39-entry item_category map are CONST-pinned here (R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-AUTHORITY-SAME-SHAPE-DRIFT-BYPASS): the item→category assignments are PRIORS, but refining one requires a REVIEWED schema+preset version bump, never a silent same-shape remap. engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval.py validates the loaded/injected authority against THIS schema at runtime, so a remap / lowered threshold fails the clean gate, not only the separate schema suite. That the map covers exactly the §13.1 numbers (the cross-ref to the separate calibration governance, which draft-07 can't express) is enforced by the eval validator + tests.
